name: m4-analyzer-11367-why
description: What does [scala/scala#11367](https://github.com/scala/scala/pull/11367) gain with one `Global`? The review's hypothesis is that a plain compile has two analyzer classes (`Global`'s, `Erasure`'s), `Duplicators` makes a third when the sources use `@specialized`, and three receivers put shared `Typer` and `Context` sites past `TypeProfileWidth=2`, into itable stubs. A local class-load log confirms `Duplicators` loads on the scala corpus and not under `-no-specialization`.

If it holds: `analyzer` beats `base` on scala, the gain goes away between `base-nospec` and `analyzer-nospec`, and scalap (no `@specialized`) is flat. On scalap the two nospec variants are extra A/As, since the flag has nothing to do there. Flame graphs: compare itable stub share. Release optimizer settings; patched JDK 26, `m4-analyzer-11367-ipc` asks the same base-against-head question with xctrace.
